newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page March 28:

RANCHO SANTA Fe, Calif. - The 39 people whose bodies were discovered inside a hilltop mansion were cultists who planned their mass suicide, videotaped farewells, packed suitcases for what they believed would be an inter-galactic trip and took their lives by ingesting a homemade recipe of drugs, applesauce and vodka.

WASHINGTON - It was a doomsday cult with computers and through the Internet it told the world exactly what it would do. The only thing left was to wait for the comet -- and the hidden spaceship -- to arrive.
WASHINGTON - The Maryland Senate approved special funds for the troubled Baltimore school system but rejected a bid to provide more money for suburban schools.
WASHINGTON - Recent changes in U.S. foreign policy and a tough new immigration law that takes effect April 1 are contributing to jeopardize the continued stay of refugees in the United States.
WASHINGTON - The National Cancer Institute recommended that women in their forties get screening mammograms for breast cancer every year or two, reversing an earlier position.
WASHINGTON - Two groups of scientists working independently have discovered a genetic defect that apparently plays a crucial role in the development of numerous kinds of cancer.

WASHINGTON - Canadian officials asserted that a Saudi man being detained in Canada over his alleged role in a bomb attack on a U.S. military residence in Saudi Arabia last year is connected to a branch of the Iranian-backed Hizbollah movement.
